transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just here because... well, my husband made me come. Him and the people at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I know they've been watching my moves. They keep changing the pallet counts on me... just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot.
How long have you been noticing that people at the warehouse have been watching you and changing the pallet counts?

I don't know... a while. I guess about eight months. That's when I really noticed them watching me and messing with my stuff. And... when I started hearing the voices, too. It's been about eight months of all that.
When you hear these voices, what do they say to you? Do they give you commands, or do they comment on what you're doing?

It's... just this man's voice. I'll be in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes, and I hear him. Clear as day. He just says, "Nicole, check it again." And there's never anybody around.

When your husband and the people at work tell you that you might be experiencing something unusual, what do you think about that? Do you think there's any possibility they might be right, or are you completely certain that everything you're experiencing is real?

I... I already told you. They just want to act like I'm crazy. But I'm not. 

I know what I see. I know they're watching my moves and... and messing with the counts. They're just saying all that to cover it up, so I don't get that supervisor spot. I'm not imagining it. It's real.

Nicole, when you hear that man's voice telling you to 'check it again,' do you ever wonder if that voice might be coming from your own mind, or are you completely certain it's someone else speaking to you from outside your head?

I don't... it's not my mind. Like I just said, I hear it clear as day. I'll be in the aisle or just folding clothes and he tells me... Nicole, check it again. There is nobody near me when it happens, but I hear him. It's a real voice. I don't really know what else to say about it.

Over these past eight months, have you been able to keep working at the warehouse and handle your responsibilities at home, or has this situation made it hard for you to do your job or take care of things?

I'm still working, but... things are different. My supervisors actually took me off the forklift. And some of the other safety stuff we do. They said my counts and... my routines were slowing the line down. 

And at home... I don't know. My husband just complains. He says he can't rely on me the way he used to. So... yeah. I guess it's been a little hard.

When you first started noticing that people at work were watching you and changing the pallet counts eight months ago, had you already been hearing that man's voice before that started, or did the voice start around the same time?
I... I think it was around the same time. The voice and... noticing what they were doing with the pallets and watching me. It's all been going on for about eight months now.

When you think back to eight months ago, did the voice and the feeling that people were watching you start suddenly—like over just a few days—or did they gradually build up over a longer period of time?
I don't really know. I guess... maybe it just sort of happened. I can't really remember if it was all at once or not. It's just been going on for a while.

When you think about those first few days or that first week when you started noticing the voice and the watching—did it all come on very suddenly, like within a day or two, or was it more gradual over several weeks before it really became noticeable?
I... I really don't know. Like I said, I can't remember exactly how it started. I wasn't... I wasn't keeping track of the days back then. It just sort of became how things are.

In the months before you first started hearing that voice and noticing people watching you, did you notice any changes in yourself? Like, were you sleeping differently, feeling more anxious or suspicious about things, or having any unusual thoughts—even before the voice started?

I don't really know about my sleep. But... I guess it's all been going on for about ten months, really. Just... the arguments got worse back then. It was right after I started trying for the shift-supervisor role. That's... that's when things started to change, I guess.

When you think back to around ten months ago when things started to change after you applied for the supervisor role, over how many weeks or months did it take before you were really noticing the voice and the watching—was it something you noticed clearly within the first week or two, or did it take several weeks to build up to where you really became aware of it?

I mean... I already told you, I don't really know how fast it all started. I just know the voice and... the feeling of being watched, people messing with things... it's been going on for about eight months. That's all I know.

Looking back to when this all started around ten months ago, when you first heard that voice or felt like people were watching you—did it happen suddenly, like you woke up one day and it was there, or did it come on gradually over weeks where it got worse and worse?

I... I don't know how else to answer that. Like I just said, I don't know if it was sudden or slow. I wasn't paying attention like that. I didn't just wake up and write it down, it just... started. That's all I remember.

You mentioned things changed after you applied for the supervisor role about ten months ago. From the day you applied for that position until the day you clearly remember hearing that man's voice for the first time—was that a matter of days, or was it weeks or months in between?
I... I don't really know. It's just a blur. I applied for the job, and then... sometime later, the voice was there. I don't know exactly how long it was between the two.

Let me ask this a different way. When you first heard that man's voice telling you to check it again, had you already been feeling like people were watching you for a while before that, or did you start hearing the voice and feeling watched around the same time?
I don't know... I think... maybe it was around the same time. I just remember it all happening. I didn't keep track of which came first.

Nicole, I know you've said you're not entirely sure about the timing. But thinking back as best you can—from when you first noticed something was off to when the voice and the feeling of being watched became really clear and unmistakable, would you say that happened over the course of just a few days, or did it take several weeks for it to build up to that point?
I... I really can't say. I just... I don't remember it like that. It's too hard to think back that far and put a timeline on it. I just know it happened.

Nicole, when you first started experiencing all of this—the voice and the feeling of being watched—did it feel like something that came on you suddenly and intensely, or did it feel more like something that crept up on you slowly over time?
I... I don't know how to explain it. Like I said, it's all just a blur. I can't really tell you if it was fast or slow. It just... it was just happening. I really don't know.

Nicole, I understand it's hard to remember exactly. But if you had to choose—when this all started, did it feel more like something that hit you suddenly and intensely over just a few days, or more like something that slowly crept up on you over many weeks?
I... I really don't want to guess. I don't know. It's just... it's too much to try and figure out right now. I don't know which one it was.

Nicole, when you first started hearing that voice and feeling watched, did it feel shocking or surprising to you—like something completely new and unexpected—or did it feel more like you were just noticing something that had already been happening around you?
I don't really know. I wasn't... I don't think I was paying attention to how it felt. It was just there. I really can't explain it any better than I already did.

Nicole, I know you've had trouble pinpointing the exact timing. But think about it this way: was there a specific week—even if you can't remember the exact day—when you suddenly felt very different from how you normally feel, or did things just gradually shift without you noticing a clear change point?
I just... I don't know. I can't remember a specific week or... or anything like that. It's just too blurry. I don't know when it changed. I just don't.

Nicole, let me ask you this directly: Before you started hearing that voice and feeling watched ten months ago, were you functioning completely normally at work and at home—no problems at all—and then things changed? Or had you already been feeling off or having some difficulties before the voice started?

I... I don't really know how to answer that. I wasn't really keeping track of how I was doing at work or... or at home. I just went to work and came back. I don't know if I was feeling off before. I just don't remember it like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: Nicole presents with acute-onset psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) with clear temporal relationship to a psychosocial stressor (applying for supervisor role ~10 months ago). The 8-month duration of prominent symptoms, acute presentation without clear prodrome, functional impairment, and absence of evidence for chronic deterioration characteristic of schizophrenia support a diagnosis of Brief Psychotic Disorder with marked stressor. While F20.0 (Paranoid Schizophrenia) remains differential due to the presence of systematized delusions and command hallucinations, the relatively acute onset, preserved insight capacity (husband/work concerns penetrate her conviction somewhat), and clear psychosocial precipitant favor the acute psychotic disorder diagnosis.

confirmed_symptoms: Auditory hallucinations: hears a man's voice saying 'Nicole, check it again' when alone
Persecutory delusions: believes coworkers are watching her moves and deliberately changing pallet counts to prevent promotion
Delusions of reference: interprets workplace behavior as targeted at her to sabotage supervisor opportunity
Removed from forklift and safety duties at work due to slowed counts and routines
Husband reports decreased reliability in household responsibilities
Acknowledged difficulties managing job and home responsibilities

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms present for approximately 8 months with psychosocial stressor (supervisor application) occurring ~10 months ago; onset timing remains unclear (patient unable to specify whether acute or gradual).
additional_requirements: Clear psychosocial stressor identified: applied for supervisor role ~10 months ago, coinciding with onset of symptoms
Prominent psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) present for 8 months
Functional impairment documented in occupational and social domains
Lack of clear prodromal period documented
Relatively preserved reality testing capacity (acknowledges others' concerns, though maintains conviction in delusions)
